cap: Menopause questions are solved by matching the presentation to a first move. Under 40 with a high FSH is primary ovarian insufficiency, tested with a karyotype and FMR1 CGG-repeat analysis. Missed periods at 42 need an hCG first. Hot flashes with a uterus need estrogen plus a progestogen; with breast cancer, a nonhormonal drug that spares CYP2D6 on tamoxifen. Vaginal dryness alone needs low-dose vaginal estradiol, and for postmenopausal bleeding, ACOG advises both ultrasound and endometrial sampling at the first evaluation for most patients (as of 2026).
